description: Soy estudiante de Ingeniería en Sistemas y me interesa usar tecnología y datos para resolver problemas ambientales. Propongo EarthAtlas.01: integrar datos MODIS y VIIRS para visualizar puntos calientes y comunicar dónde y cuándo se detecta actividad. Puedo aportar programación, ideas, organización y documentación. Busco personas interesadas en análisis de datos, mapas/GIS, desarrollo web, diseño o medioambiente. ¡Sumate para crear una solución creativa y global!
summary: EarthAtlas helps people identify when thermal activity is unusually high. It integrates NASA FIRMS records from MODIS and VIIRS into a historical calendar for a pilot area near Santa Cruz, Bolivia. Users can compare observed with harmonized values, see how a month ranks against the same months in other years, and export the underlying series. A separate global map shows recent satellite detections with their coordinates and acquisition details. EarthAtlas makes satellite transitions and estimated values visible so land managers, students and researchers can interpret seasonal patterns with the data limitations in view.
details:
MODIS and VIIRS have different detection characteristics, so a change in sensor can look like a change in fire activity. EarthAtlas uses the PYRA historical pipeline to filter NASA FIRMS detections and aggregate them on an H3 grid. The main metric counts hotspot-days, with each cell contributing at most once per day within a sensor series. Overlapping satellite records support calibration to the Suomi NPP VIIRS reference scale. The app preserves observed values, labels the early Aqua MODIS segment as estimated, and distinguishes provisional near-real-time data from completed historical months.

The pilot archive covers August 2002 through October 2026 near Santa Cruz, Bolivia. Users can switch between observed and harmonized series, inspect the seasonal calendar, compare a month against the same calendar month in other years, and export CSV data. In the pilot archive, September 2019 recorded 251 harmonized hotspot-days, about 2.8 times the median for other Septembers. The separate worldwide map shows recent detections and their location, acquisition time, satellite and fire radiative power when available. Historical harmonization covers the pilot area. Hotspot-days describe detected thermal activity. Burned area, severity and ignition causes require separate evidence.

EarthAtlas combines a React and TypeScript interface, Leaflet maps, Python and FastAPI services, and the PYRA processing stack, including H3, DuckDB and Parquet. Docker packages the application. The paired archive and monitoring views let users move from a historical pattern to geographic context, while the exports and provenance labels support independent review.
